author: Yaja Nowakowski
text:
Hi Sue. I don't know where in the world you're located, but do know that some phones aren't fully compatible with the FreeStyle Libre 2 app. 

Here in Australia, the mobile phone I had at the time I was diagnosed, was not included on the Abbot compatibility list. It meant I had to buy another phone. My mobile provider found a phone that accepts the Libre app. 

However, when I began using it, the alarm would go off every few minutes, including overnight. There were also incessant reminders that it could not connect to the sensor. I thought it may have been the sensor that was the issue, and so I replaced it with a new one and reinstalled the app. 

Sadly, it only helped partially, i.e. the alarm going off stopped, but the disconnection and FMC connection errors continued. I found out from Abbott that my new phone had not been fully tested, which is why it wasn't on their list. 

So after lots of searching, I found a phone that's now compatible, which they'll send once they receive the one I puchased initially. Hoping it will be an improvement. 

What I'm actually saying Sue, is for you to make sure your phone is compatible. Many mobile devices can download the app. The down side is that many of those have not been fully tested, or tested at all.

All the best, Sue.

author: Rick Fritz
text:
Abbott tested several insertion locations to achieve the best results during the clinical trial years ago.  Their primary goal was to obtain FDA approval of the product in order to commercialize it, therefore, back of arm is where they showed FDA the best results of all locations they tested.

Sometimes, manufacturers conduct post-approval trials (phase 4), but not clear if Abbott spend the time and money on further testing.  Usually, manufacturers don’t like to further test a product once FDA approved fearing additional testing results may be in conflict of the original testing results that granted FDA approval.
